_comment: GDPR/UK GDPR Art. 13 is a notice-at-collection duty: a tool that sends something to our server has to say so, in the tool, at the moment of the send. Not in a policy three clicks away. cmp-collection-notice-present requires every tool that talks to /api/ to render one of the strings registered here. Registering a string is not a formality — read it and ask whether a visitor would feel misled after reading it and then learning what the request carries.
_matching: `file` is the tool component. `must` is a distinctive substring of the disclosure it renders; the check fails if that substring is no longer in the file, which is what stops a refactor from quietly deleting the sentence.
_notice: The site-wide notice route is separate: the check requires a page under app/ whose route contains 'privacy' and which the footer links from every built page. It does not exist yet — see the finding.

tools.sends: the URL you type, to /scan-url; our server then loads that page
tools.must: The site sees a visit from our server.

tools.sends: the short link you paste, to /scan-url, to be followed server-side
tools.must: Our server opens the link and shows you the address it redirects to.
